subject: Economics
description: Replacement of Planning Commission, structure, indices, Aspirational Districts

questions.stem: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission with effect from:
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was set up by a Cabinet Resolution dated 1 January 2015 — replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission (established 1950). Both are NON-statutory and NON-constitutional bodies — created by executive resolution, not law. The 12th Five Year Plan (2012-17) was the last under the Planning Commission. Five Year Plans were ended after the 12th plan; replaced by 15-year Vision, 7-year Strategy and 3-year Action Agenda.

questions.stem: The ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog is the:
questions.explanation: PM is ex-officio Chairperson. Vice-Chairperson — appointed by PM (currently Suman K. Bery; previously Rajiv Kumar, Arvind Panagariya). Other components — CEO (currently B.V.R. Subrahmanyam), Full-time Members, Part-time Members (rotating from premier institutions), Ex-officio Members (4 Union Ministers nominated by PM), Special Invitees, Governing Council (PM + all CMs + LG of UTs with assemblies).

questions.stem: The 'Aspirational Districts Programme' launched by NITI Aayog in January 2018 covers:

options.option_text: 112 most under-developed districts identified across 28 states

questions.explanation: Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) — launched 5 January 2018 by PM Modi. 112 districts ranked across 49 KPIs in 5 sectors — Health & Nutrition (30%), Education (30%), Agriculture & Water Resources (20%), Financial Inclusion & Skill Development (10%), Basic Infrastructure (10%). Monthly 'Champions of Change' rankings drive a healthy competition. Real-time tracking via the Champions of Change Dashboard. Building on its success, NITI launched the Aspirational Blocks Programme (Jan 2023) covering 500 blocks.

questions.stem: Which index — published by NITI Aayog — measures progress of states across 17 SDGs adopted by India?
questions.explanation: SDG India Index — first published 2018 (baseline), then 2019, 2020-21, 2023-24. Developed jointly with UN India. States are scored 0-100 across 17 SDGs and given a composite score; categorised into Achiever (≥100), Front Runner (65-99), Performer (50-64), Aspirant (<50). Kerala has been the consistent topper. Other NITI indices — Composite Water Management Index, Health Index, Education Quality Index, Innovation Index, Export Preparedness Index, Multidimensional Poverty Index (national).

questions.stem: The first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog (2015-17) was:
questions.explanation: Arvind Panagariya (Columbia Univ) — first VC, 2015-17. Succeeded by Rajiv Kumar (2017-22), Suman K. Bery (May 2022 onwards). Currently Panagariya chairs the 16th Finance Commission (2023). Bibek Debroy chaired the EAC-PM. CEOs of NITI: Sindhushree Khullar (1st, 2015-16), Amitabh Kant (2016-22), Parameswaran Iyer (2022-23), B.V.R. Subrahmanyam (Mar 2023 onwards).

questions.stem: The two main 'Hubs' that form the operational backbone of NITI Aayog are the:

options.option_text: Team India Hub and Knowledge & Innovation Hub

questions.explanation: Team India Hub — the cooperative-federalism arm; engages with states, ministries, sectoral matters. Knowledge & Innovation Hub — think-tank arm; research, policy reviews, future-of-work, AI for All, Atal Innovation Mission, Atal Tinkering Labs. AIM was launched 2016; over 10,000 ATLs in schools by 2024. NITI's three pillars: cooperative federalism, competitive federalism (state rankings), bottom-up planning.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does NOT have the power to:

options.option_text: Conduct policy research and offer recommendations
Engage state governments through the Governing Council

questions.explanation: Key structural shift — NITI Aayog has NO fund-allocation power; that role moved entirely to the Finance Ministry (Department of Expenditure) and the Finance Commission. The Planning Commission used to allocate Plan funds to states (Plan vs Non-Plan distinction also abolished). NITI is now purely advisory + collaborative — a 'think-tank'. This decoupling was meant to remove the perceived imposition of Centre's plans on states.
